response.overview: As industrial unrest swept Britain in the early 1980s, a state-funded oral history group set out to record life and work in the wool textile capital of Bradford. The materials they left behind — photographic negatives, reel-to-reel tapes and a mass of archival papers — form the basis of this immersive road movie through the present-day city. Playing out as a series of encounters with sensory fragments of social history, Bradford Forwards and Backwards explores a strange threshold in industrial time, and stands as a singular meditation on post-industrial experience.
response.tagline: A film about sensory history and postindustrial change in the north of England.
response.title: Bradford Forwards and Backwards
